vo: Your full-size crib rule changed August first.
Myth: the crib standard stays put. Since August first, twenty twenty-six, part twelve-nineteen cites the twenty twenty-five ASTM version.
Each full-size crib must meet it. Before, it was twenty nineteen.
Say your crib file still shows only the twenty nineteen standard. Check it.
Comment M and Z, we'll DM you the free CPSC finder.
caption:
Full-size crib sellers: 16 CFR 1219.2 changed on August 1, 2026.
It now requires each full-size baby crib to comply with ASTM F1169-25. Before that date, the rule cited ASTM F1169-19.
If your test reports and certificate file still point only to the 2019 version, check them against the current rule.
The certificate still lists each applicable rule separately (16 CFR 1110.11(a)(2)).
Not sure which rules apply? Comment M&Z and we'll DM you the free CPSC Finder.

sources.quote: Each full-size baby crib must comply with all applicable provisions of ASTM F1169-25, Standard Consumer Safety Specification for Full-Size Baby Cribs, approved December 15, 2025.

Link to an amendment published at 91 FR 23913, May 4, 2026. Each full-size baby crib must comply with all applicable provisions of ASTM F1169-19, Standard Consumer Safety Specification for Full-Size Baby Cribs approved March 15, 2019.
Finished product certificates must identify separately all applicable rules, bans, standards, or regulations.
